signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Weekend Tariff Escalation
signals.text: Trump's weekend threat of Section 301 tariffs on the EU drives safe-haven demand into the Greenback while the Franc remains the G10 laggard. The 1.260% G10 performance spread favors USD upside as markets absorb the war premium and tariff risks. The next Fed meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 July is the primary catalyst for confirming this USD dominance against the CHF yield disadvantage.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + COT Squeeze
signals.text: JPY COT net short -114k (26.7% long) creates short-squeeze risk (USD/JPY downside if shorts cover) as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and $92 WTI oil trigger global risk-off flows. Despite the +266bp OIS carry advantage for USD, JPY's positive ESI (+13.5) and the Nikkei's 2.73% Friday slide signal a move toward the SMA20 at 162.41. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 31 July serves as the definitive catalyst for JPY's recovery path.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Tariff Risk + ESI Underperformance
signals.text: EUR COT net short -80.5k reinforces a bearish bias as Trump targets the EU with new tariff threats while the Eurozone ESI remains at a strong negative -15.0. Weak relative data and persistent misses limit the impact of the ECB's hiking bias, keeping the pair pinned below the SMA200 (1.1639). The ECB meeting on 10 September is the catalyst for any shift in this bearish structural trend.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Carry Compression + BoE Event Risk
signals.text: GBP COT net long +33.8k (66.3% long) faces liquidation risk as the -9bp OIS carry disadvantage and weekend risk-off sentiment weigh on the pound. The pair closed Friday at 1.3321, positioned below all major SMAs (20, 50, 200), signaling technical exhaustion. The BoE meeting on 30 July is the catalyst for determining if the current hold bias can sustain the crowded long positioning.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Unwind Risk
signals.text: AUD COT net long +20.5k (62.8% long) creates downside risk if the pair breaks its tight 8-day range support at 0.6961. While the +71bp OIS carry advantage and RBA hike bias (11 Aug) provide a floor, an extreme retail short bias in AUD/CHF (96%) suggests professional longs is likely to be vulnerable to a broader risk-off flush. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 21% hike priced) on 11 August determines the longevity of the AUD yield advantage.
